summary: The prepared_gaia variant is a design-plus-code Python/CrewAI system with a richer role decomposition than the other variants, including department, opinion, price, customer, and reporter agents. Its implementation is mostly prompt/task scaffolding: it hardcodes the property address, provides no concrete source adapters or tools, and returns a mock string when crew execution fails. Because core functional requirements are not implemented beyond task descriptions, this variant is not ready as a working system.

findings.description: The user-address requirement is not implemented as runtime input; the main workflow uses one hardcoded address.
Investment, opinion, and price capabilities are represented as CrewAI task prompts rather than implemented retrieval logic or source-specific tools.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/tasks.py:23-30 describes researching planned investments, lines 42-48 describe gathering opinions, and lines 60-68 describe price comparison; no corresponding concrete API/tool implementation is provided.

findings.description: The design identifies specialized roles for departments, review platforms, price platforms, customer, and reporter.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/README.md:15-36 lists 13 specialized agents, including department agents, opinion agents, and price comparison agents.

findings.description: The documented execution model says agents run in parallel, but the implementation configures sequential execution.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/README.md:41 says all agents start their tasks in parallel; prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:106 sets process=Process.sequential.

findings.description: Execution failures are masked by returning a mock result, so callers can receive a successful-looking value after the real workflow fails.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:120-125 catches Exception, prints a mock-result message, and returns "Mock result for demonstration purposes".

findings.description: The reporter task depends on other tasks conceptually, but the interfaces are only natural-language task descriptions and not typed data contracts or validated schemas.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/tasks.py:75-86 defines reporter_task with context_tasks and expected prose output, but no structured input or output schema.

missing_requirements: Runtime apartment search using a user-provided address.
Implemented retrieval of planned investments from multiple public-office sources.
Implemented retrieval of local-service opinions from multiple review services.
Implemented comparison against current offers from multiple real-estate listing services.
A final report generated from validated collected data rather than task prompts or fallback mock output.
logical_inconsistencies: README.md says all agents run in parallel, while main.py configures Process.sequential.
The system presents source-specific agents such as Google, Booking, OLX, Otodom, and Allegro, but no source-specific integration logic exists.
The workflow returns a mock success value after catching any crew execution exception.
implementation_risks: The system can hallucinate or fabricate external-source data because retrieval is delegated to LLM prompts rather than implemented connectors.
The hardcoded address prevents evaluating arbitrary properties without code changes.
The broad exception handler hides real execution failures and makes downstream success/failure detection unreliable.
No tests are present for the prepared_gaia implementation.
